what_its_for: Pimozide is used to help control motor and vocal tics (sudden, repeated movements or sounds you cannot control) in people with Tourette's syndrome. It is usually used when other treatments have not worked well enough. It belongs to a group of medicines called antipsychotics.
how_to_take: Take pimozide by mouth exactly as your doctor tells you. You can take it with or without food. Try to take it at the same time each day to keep a steady level in your body. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Do not crush or chew the tablet. Do not stop taking this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor first, as this can cause withdrawal symptoms.
dosing: Your doctor will start you on a low dose and slowly increase it to find the right amount for you. Most adults start at 1 to 2 mg per day and the dose may be increased gradually. The usual maximum dose is 10 mg per day (or 0.2 mg per kilogram of body weight per day, whichever is lower). Children are usually started on lower doses. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions for your dose.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store pimozide tablets at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C and 25°C). Keep the medicine away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medicine after the expiration date on the package. Ask your pharmacist how to safely dispose of any unused medicine.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking grapefruit juice while taking pimozide, as it can increase the amount of medicine in your blood and raise your risk of side effects. Do not drink alcohol, as it can increase drowsiness and dizziness. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how this medicine affects you, since it can cause drowsiness, dizziness, or blurred vision. Tell all of your doctors and dentist that you take pimozide before starting any new medicines, since many common drugs (including antibiotics like clarithromycin and azithromycin, antidepressants, antifungals, and some heart medicines) can cause a dangerous interaction with pimozide. Avoid overheating and dehydration, especially in hot weather or during exercise, as pimozide can affect your body's ability to regulate temperature.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the nearest emergency room if you experience: a fast, irregular, or pounding heartbeat or chest pain (this could be a sign of a serious heart rhythm problem called QT prolongation); sudden stiffness, high fever, sweating, or confusion (signs of a rare but serious condition called Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome); uncontrolled muscle movements in your face, tongue, or body that are new (a condition called tardive dyskinesia); severe dizziness or fainting; difficulty breathing or swallowing; unusual thoughts, depression, or thoughts of harming yourself; a skin rash or signs of allergic reaction such as swelling of the face, lips, or throat. Also call your doctor if you notice increased or new unusual movements or tics, significant weight gain, or if your symptoms do not improve.
when_it_works: Pimozide does not work immediately. It may take several weeks — usually 2 to 4 weeks or longer — before you notice a significant improvement in your tics. Be patient and keep taking it as prescribed even if you do not notice changes right away. Your doctor will check your progress regularly and adjust your dose if needed.
special_populations: Children: Pimozide can be used in children aged 12 and older for Tourette's syndrome. Children are more sensitive to the medicine, so lower doses are used. Regular monitoring is very important. Older adults (65+): Older adults are more sensitive to side effects such as dizziness, falls, and heart rhythm problems. Extra care and lower doses may be needed. Pregnancy: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Pimozide may cause problems for a newborn if taken during the third trimester. The risks and benefits must be carefully discussed with your doctor. Breastfeeding: It is not known if pimozide passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding while on this medicine. Liver or kidney disease: If you have liver or kidney problems, tell your doctor, as dose adjustments may be needed.
